title: Root words and their word families
examples: What does the root port mean?
How do I work out a long word?

explain.say: Picture a plate that will not break, even if you drop it. We can call it unbreakable. Look at the middle chunk on the board: break. That is the root word, the heart of the word.

draw.text: Root words and their word families

explain.say: Now the front chunk lights up: un, a prefix that means not. Put them together: un plus break means not break. Can you guess what the last chunk adds?
See able glowing at the end? It means can be. So unbreakable means cannot be broken. Once you spot the root and its helpers, even huge words get easy. Try uncomfortable!
Now look at the web on the board. In the middle is the root act, which means do. Around it is its family: actor, action, react, active. Every word keeps act inside it. Which one means to act back?
Brilliant detective work! Some roots come from Latin. Look at the board: port means carry. Transport carries things across, a porter carries bags. Challenge: what can a portable speaker do?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: trans means across, port means carry

faq.a: A root word is the main part of a word that carries its meaning. You can add prefixes and suffixes to it, like un and able in unbreakable.
A word family is a group of words that share the same root, like act, actor, action and react. If you know one, you can guess the others.

faq.q: What does the root port mean?
faq.a: Port comes from the Latin portare, to carry. Transport, export, import, portable and porter all have something to do with carrying.

faq.q: How do I work out a long word?
faq.a: Split it into prefix, root and suffix, and work out each part. Invisible is in, not, plus vis, see, plus ible, able to be: not able to be seen.
asks: How do roots help with hard words?

faq.q: Are all root words from Latin?
faq.a: No. Many come from Latin and Greek, like port and graph, but everyday roots like break, help and play come from Old English.

facts: Graph comes from the Greek for write: autograph, paragraph and photograph all share it.
Vis comes from the Latin for see, as in vision, visible and visit.

quiz.say: The root aud means hear. What is an audience?
quiz.show: The root aud means hear. What is an audience?
quiz.why: An audience hears or listens to a show.
